messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered: high error rate and GPU OOMs in prod-us-west-2 serving pool (route: /v1/generate). Incident severity: S3. Paging on-call.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by Mateo Rivera.

Mateo Rivera: I'm on it — grabbing logs and stack traces now. Can someone check autoscaler events and node churn?

Priya Singh: Seeing a pattern: rapid node add/remove over the last 8m. kube-events show repeated nodes joining then quickly becoming NotReady -> drained -> terminated. Looks like autoscaler is reacting to bursty queue and then snapback.

Priya Singh: Logs from a sample pod (OOM/crashloop):
```
[2026-03-15T10:17:34Z] Error: CUDA out of memory when allocating 234375000 bytes
2026-03-15T10:17:34Z] runtime: oomkilled, status=137
2026-03-15T10:17:35Z] Container crashed, restarting (CrashLoopBackOff)
```

Dan O'Neill: Node metrics: GPU memory utilization spiked to 98% on new nodes immediately after provisioning. Then kube-proxy health flaps during termination. I suspect the autoscaler is overprovisioning small batches then mass-evicting when spot preemption or scaling decisions occur.

Alice Chen: Confirmed correlated with a traffic burst from a client job that started ~10:16. Queue depth hit our max-concurrency and spawned many model workers. Autoscaler took min-replicas -> scaled to desired=48 -> then back down to 8 in ~90s. That's the oscillation.

Laura Gomez: Customer impact: some 3rd-party clients saw increased latency (500s) and ~7% request errors for ~12m. A handful of paying customers reported timeouts; CS triage is collecting request ids.

Mateo Rivera: Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) Suspend autoscaling for the pool (set desired replicas to current stable), 2) Route traffic away from the pool to dedicated fallback models with smaller memory footprints, 3) Temporarily increase GPU eviction grace and set node autoscaler cooldown. Which do we want first?

Priya Singh: Do 1 + 2. Suspend autoscale and pin the pool (disable scale-to-zero and scale-up for now). Also push a routing rule to send new traffic to model:small-quantized-v2. That lowers memory per worker and should reduce OOMs.

Dan O'Neill: Commands I'm running now:
```
# cordon and set desired replicas
kubectl annotate nodepool prod-us-west-2-serving autoscaler.k8s.io/disabled=true --overwrite
kubectl patch deployment redwood-serving -p '{"spec":{"replicas":12}}' --namespace=prod
# add taint to prevent new pods from landing on flaky nodes
kubectl taint nodes node-xyz temporary-taint=autoscale:NoSchedule || true
```

Priya Singh: Routing change: pushing a short-lived policy to route 30% of traffic to small-quantized-v2 and 70% to current. Applying canary immediately.

Incident Bot: deployment rollout started by Priya Singh. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Mateo Rivera: I'm updating PagerDuty notes and doing a handoff to on-call infra. Mateo -> Dan. Dan, take lead on node churn investigation.

Dan O'Neill: Acknowledged. I'll dig into cloud-provider scaling logs. If we see spot preemption bursts, we'll switch to on-demand node group for the short term.

Alice Chen: Also adding jitter to the autoscaler config: increase scaleDownDelaySeconds from 60 -> 300, and reduce scaleUpAggression (policy: stabilize-window 5m). That should smooth oscillations.

Priya Singh: Patch ready for runtime: add defensive eviction for model worker if GPU memory > 92% to avoid OOMs and add retry backoff. Rolling to 20% of pods.

Laura Gomez: Customer comms: drafting a short status update — will say limited errors and increased latency for ~12m, mitigation in progress, we will follow up with root cause and timeline.

Dan O'Neill: Found cloud autoscaler events: multiple provisioning requests failed due to instance quota checks; autoscaler retried and created many small instances across AZs which triggered pod rescheduling. There's also a race where new nodes attach GPUs then kubelet restart causes pods to be rescheduled causing duplicates in GPU allocation.

Priya Singh: That explains why GPU memory spikes immediately — duplicate model workers probed the same GPU capacity. Ok switching the pool to single-AZ for stability and setting max surge for rolling updates to 1.

Mateo Rivera: Status update for PD notes: mitigation applied: autoscale suspended, routing adjusted to smaller model, nodepool pinned, small runtime patch rolling. Monitoring for 15m.

Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: Alert update: error rate decreased ~85% after routing change and suspend. Continuing to monitor.

Alice Chen: Postmortem checklist items coming: - add autoscaler cooldown default to 3m - add quota check gating before autoscale - implement node attach sanity check for GPU readiness - add model fallback routes to console UI - restore CS list of affected requests for follow-up.

Priya Singh: Also adding an immediate hotfix: if scale events > 3 within 10m, veto further scale-ups for that pool for 10m. I'll open a PR after this incident.

Laura Gomez: Sending update to affected customers: ETA for root cause analysis 48 hours. Will include mitigation timeline and any ID tokens for failed requests.

Dan O'Neill: I'll keep the nodepool in stabilized mode and watch GPU attach logs for the next hour. If anything regresses I'll re-route all traffic to dedicated CPU fallback.

Mateo Rivera: Thanks team — handing back to oncall rotation at 11:00. If anyone sees error rates climb past threshold (0.5% errors or >200ms p95 increase), page infra oncall.

Incident Bot: Incident status: monitoring. All messages in this thread have been archived to the incident ticket #INC-2026-452.

Laura Gomez: :thumbsup: I'll follow up with a post-incident update and coordinate the RCA next steps.

Priya Singh: Opening follow-up tasks now: PR for autoscaler cooldown, runtime patch PR, routing console flag.

Mateo Rivera: Closing handoff — marked operationally mitigated at 10:58. Final follow-up actions assigned.

Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: Incident resolved to monitored state.
